title: Market Research Foundations Adventure
welcome_lead: You'll compare primary vs secondary research and meet the main data-gathering tools.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies market research foundations — primary vs secondary research methods.
final_note: You can distinguish primary from secondary research and list the main methods of each.

concepts.def: Gathering info on customers and the market
First-hand data collected by the firm itself
Data already collected by someone else
List of set questions to gather data
Small group discusses a product or topic

walkthroughs.body_html:
Primary data is collected first-hand — specific to your question.

Methods: questionnaires, interviews, observation, focus groups. Accurate but costly and slow.

Secondary data exists already — gov stats, news, industry reports, internet.

Cheap and fast but may be out of date or not perfectly relevant.

Start with secondary for the big picture, then use primary for specific gaps.

Most firms combine both to balance cost, speed and reliability.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary market research?
options: The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.
Primary research is the most important and secondary research is less important.
Primary research is done first and secondary research is done later.
Primary research is original data the business gathers itself (surveys, interviews); secondary research uses existing data (reports, government statistics, market intelligence).

mcqs.q: Which sector does manufacturing belong to?
options: Manufacturing is in the tertiary sector along with services.
The secondary sector — which transforms raw materials from the primary sector (farming, mining) into finished goods.
The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.
Manufacturing is in the primary sector because it makes things.

mcqs.q: What are the four Ps of the marketing mix?
options: Product, Price, Place (distribution), and Promotion — the controllable variables a business uses to satisfy customers and achieve objectives.
The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.
The four Ps are Product, Price, Profit, and People.
Primary research is done first and secondary research is done later.
